context: Sam Reed is applying to coordinate volunteers at a neighbourhood food pantry. At the end of the interview the panel receives two pages about a Saturday delivery Sam organised. The first is a cover sheet for the funder. The second is an entry the volunteers wrote after the shift. Both reviewers have both pages. Each has been asked to cite the one page that best explains their assessment.
rule: Leadership means giving people clear responsibilities and adjusting the plan when something goes wrong. You are deciding whether the panel has evidence of those actions.
walk: Start with the cover. A contact name tells Reviewer A whom to call. It leaves the division of work unanswered. Now read the diary verbs: gave, asked, reassigned. Reviewer B can point to the very actions A wanted to see. Both used the same leadership standard. A change of source explains the different strength of their judgments.
